planting.note: Broadcast seed in spring onto raw gypsum or alkaline flat soil in full sun; this low, dioecious sod-grass needs bare mineral ground to establish and resents competition from taller companions.

directions: Burrograss is a short, wiry, stoloniferous grass native to the alkaline and gypsum flats and heavily trafficked desert grassland soils of the Chihuahuan Desert, where it forms low sod-like mats rather than upright tufts. Male and female plants are separate, with female plants producing small, spiny burr-like seed clusters low on the stem that catch on passing animals for dispersal across the flat, open ground it favors. Its tight, grazing-tolerant mat makes it useful for stabilizing bare, saline, or gypsum-rich soil where taller bunchgrasses struggle to compete, and it stays low enough to read as a groundcover rather than an ornamental grass. It needs no supplemental water once established and is best kept out of irrigated, fertile beds where faster-growing grasses will shade it out.

planting.note: Direct-sow in spring into gypsum or alkaline flat soil in a wash, swale, or other spot that collects occasional runoff; vine mesquite spreads from long above-ground stolons rather than seed once established.

directions: Vine mesquite is a warm-season perennial grass of Chihuahuan Desert gypsum and alkaline flats, washes, and swales, where its long, wiry, above-ground stolons root at the nodes and knit together into a dense, mat-forming sod. Unlike the straight bunchgrasses of drier gypsum ridges, it concentrates in the slightly lower, moisture-collecting microsites of a gypsum flat, making it a useful indicator of where runoff briefly pools after storms. The narrow, upright seed stalks carry small, tightly packed spikelets above the sprawling foliage mat in summer, giving it a two-layered look distinct from typical dryland bunchgrasses. Plant it in a wash-like depression or seasonally wet-dry gravel garden where its stolons can spread freely, since it declines when confined or kept in rich, consistently moist soil.
